59408267.s: The museum houses a large collection of important heritage pieces. Next to the museum on the same floor is a large library with many of the most important books on history and culture. The pieces are displayed in an excellent, scholarly manner that attracts tourists, through valuable wooden frames designed as small wings and glass cabinets, which received great attention from Sheikh Abdulaziz Omar Makwar.

59408265.t: Muhammad the Messenger of Allah Exhibition
59408265.s: The Muhammad the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) Exhibition, which will open its doors for a full year, includes more than 150 illustrative panels about aspects of the life of the noble Messenger, may the best of prayers be upon him: his birth, his noble lineage, his physical and moral attributes, his relationship with his Lord, his relationship with his family, and the names and number of his wives.
59408265.b:
The Muhammad the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) Exhibition, which will open its doors for a full year, includes more than 150 illustrative panels about aspects of the life of the noble Messenger, may the best of prayers be upon him: his birth, his noble lineage, his physical and moral attributes, his relationship with his Lord, his relationship with his family, and the names and number of his wives,

the number of his sons and daughters, his companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and his migration to Madinah.

59408205.s: The complex has several components that serve local people and visitors: the Arabic Calligraphy Centre, the art gallery and the educational photographs and documents centre, as well as the historic theatre and the Ithar Centre for scouting and volunteer services.
59408205.b:
The complex has several components that serve local people and visitors: the Arabic Calligraphy Centre, the art gallery and the educational photographs and documents centre, as well as the historic theatre and the Ithar Centre for scouting and volunteer services.

The complex also includes a Quran memorisation institute, historical documents on education in the Madinah region going back more than 80 years, old photographs of education and its occasions in the city, a heritage public library, some antiques and archaeological items, and the records of old files used in the education departments and schools of Madinah.

59408199.s: The first and largest museum specialising in the history of Madinah and its architectural and cultural heritage. The museum illuminates the bright pages of the history of Madinah, may the best of prayers be upon its most honoured resident, and reveals the landmarks of its heritage, its Islamic civilisation and the fragrance of its glorious history. The museum aims to enrich knowledge in specialised sciences and research on the history of Madinah, and is distinguished by its display of a large collection of artefacts and models that give a vivid picture of the landmarks of Madinah's history, in addition to a huge collection of rare photographs of the city's history.

59408199.a: Safwan Ibn Malik Al Tamimi, Al Mabuth, Madinah

59408138.s: Saeed ibn Al-Aas Palace is an old archaeological palace in Wadi Al Aqiq in Madinah, built by the Companion Saeed ibn Al-Aas (may Allah be pleased with him) when he was governor of Madinah during the caliphate of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him). Saeed ibn Al-Aas was known for his justice and wisdom in governing Madinah. He took care to develop the city, building roads and homes for the people, and was among the Companions famed for generosity and good governance. The remains of this palace still bear witness to the architectural history of the Wadi Al Aqiq area in the Umayyad era, and it is one of the archaeological landmarks that attract lovers of Islamic history in Madinah.
59408138.b: Saeed ibn Al-Aas Palace is an old archaeological palace in Wadi Al Aqiq in Madinah, built by the Companion Saeed ibn Al-Aas (may Allah be pleased with him) when he was governor of Madinah during the caliphate of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him). 59408132.s: Masjid Fatimah Alzahraa, called Masjid Saad ibn Muadh in historical sources, is the smallest of the Seven Mosques, with an area of about 12 square metres and a small step, built in the same architectural style as the rest of the group. It is one of the Seven Mosques in the Khandaq area north-west of the Prophet's Mosque, which mark the positions where the Muslims were stationed and led during the Battle of the Trench (Al Ahzab) in the fifth year of the Hijra. The mosque is attributed to the noble Companion Saad ibn Muadh (may Allah be pleased with him), the chief of the Aws, who played a prominent role in that battle, and it is one of the small landmarks visitors to Madinah seek out to complete their visit to the historic Seven Mosques.

59408115.s: Masjid Al Qiblatayn holds a special place in the memory of Muslims around the world, and among those interested in Islamic history and everyone who visits Madinah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed in it, and it witnessed the change of the qiblah from Al Aqsa Mosque to the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram). It is established in the Sunnah through the Prophetic hadiths and recorded in Islamic history as one of the most important and prominent historical landmarks and one of the greatest Prophetic sites in Madinah after the Prophet's Mosque and Quba Mosque.
59408115.b: Masjid Al Qiblatayn holds a special place in the memory of Muslims around the world, and among those interested in Islamic history and everyone who visits Madinah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed in it, and it witnessed the change of the qiblah from Al Aqsa Mosque to the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram). 59408115.a: Khalid Ibn Al Walid Road, Al Qiblatayn, Madinah

59408095.s: Urwah ibn Al Zubayr Palace lies on the banks of Wadi Al Aqiq in western Madinah, along the road leading to Masjid Al Miqat (the miqat of the people of Madinah), about 3.5 km from the Prophet's Mosque. Umar ibn Abdulaziz (may Allah be pleased with him) ordered the palace to be built at the request of Urwah ibn Al Zubayr, one of the great jurists of the Tabi'un and a son of the Companion Al Zubayr ibn Al Awwam (may Allah be pleased with him), known for his wide knowledge of jurisprudence, hadith and the Prophet's biography. Some of the palace's buildings still stand today and are important archaeological landmarks reflecting the architectural style of the Umayyad era, attracting lovers of Islamic history and antiquities.
59408095.b: Urwah ibn Al Zubayr Palace lies on the banks of Wadi Al Aqiq in western Madinah, along the road leading to Masjid Al Miqat (the miqat of the people of Madinah), about 3.5 km from the Prophet's Mosque. Some of the palace's buildings still stand today and are important archaeological landmarks reflecting the architectural style of the Umayyad era, attracting lovers of Islamic history and antiquities.
59408095.a: 3521 Umar Ibn Al Khattab Road, Urwah, Madinah

59408092.s: The mosque is located south-west of the Prophet's Mosque, 455 metres from the expansion building and about 133 metres from Al Ghamamah Mosque. It stands at the junction of Quba Street and Al Anbariyah Street, on the left for those travelling from Madinah to Quba. Umar Mosque faces Quba Road on its western side and overlooks the square of Al Ghamamah Mosque on its northern side.

59408091.s: Masjid Salman Al Farsi (may Allah be pleased with him) is one of the mosques and prayer places of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) in Madinah, according to the best verified accounts, and is the second of the Seven Mosques in the Khandaq area north-west of the Prophet's Mosque. The mosque is attributed to the noble Companion Salman Al Farsi (may Allah be pleased with him), who proposed digging the trench and advised the Prophet (peace be upon him) to do so to protect Madinah from the invasion of the Confederates in the fifth year of the Hijra. It is one of the Seven Mosques that mark the command and stationing positions of the Muslims during the Battle of the Trench, and visitors to Madinah seek it out to learn the story of that enduring battle and the role of the Companions in it.
59408091.b: Masjid Salman Al Farsi (may Allah be pleased with him) is one of the mosques and prayer places of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) in Madinah, according to the best verified accounts, and is the second of the Seven Mosques in the Khandaq area north-west of the Prophet's Mosque. 59408059.s: Masjid Al Fath lies on the slope of Mount Sala, west of the Prophet's Mosque, where the tent of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was pitched on the day of the Battle of the Trench (Al Ahzab), and close to it is the cemetery of the martyrs of the Trench. It is called Al Fath (the Victory) because of the victory the Muslims achieved after the battle, and is also called the Mosque of the Confederates because the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed against the Confederates there. It is also known as the Upper Mosque because of its elevation above the surrounding mosques.

59408058.s: Masjid Al Suqya is a small mosque topped by three domes, covering an area of 56 square metres, without a minaret and with an Ottoman design. It takes its name from its proximity to the Well of Al Suqya, from which the Prophet (peace be upon him) is reported to have performed ablution on his way to the great Battle of Badr, praying near it and supplicating for the people of Madinah. Umar ibn Abdulaziz (may Allah be pleased with him), during his governorship of Madinah, later built a mosque on the spot where he prayed. The mosque was restored during the reign of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Fahd ibn Abdulaziz in 1423-1424 AH, as part of the projects to care for the historical and archaeological mosques of Madinah, so that it remains a witness to this stage of the Prophet's biography.

59408057.s: Masjid Bani Ghifar is one of the traditionally recorded archaeological mosques in which, according to reports, the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed, and it is also known as the Great Cave of Bani Haram. Its name comes from the Ghifar tribe, one of the tribes of Kinanah, many of whose members embraced Islam early and settled in this part of Madinah. The mosque bears witness to the Prophet's (peace be upon him) connection with the various neighbourhoods and tribes that lived in Madinah, as he would visit them and pray there to strengthen Islamic brotherhood among the Muhajirun, the Ansar and the Muslim tribes. It still stands today as one of the small archaeological landmarks sought out by lovers of Islamic history and the Prophet's biography in Madinah.

59408057.a: 4116 1st Ring Branch Road, Al Fath, Madinah

59408054.s: Anbariya Mosque is located west of the Prophet's Mosque, near the Hejaz Railway station of the Ottoman era, about 500 metres from it, with a northern facade. The mosque is surrounded by a circular garden that adds to its splendour, setting off its archaeological buildings, which were built in the Ottoman era of finely carved stone showing remarkable architectural skill.
59408054.b: Anbariya Mosque is located west of the Prophet's Mosque, near the Hejaz Railway station of the Ottoman era, about 500 metres from it, with a northern facade. The mosque is surrounded by a circular garden that adds to its splendour, setting off its archaeological buildings, which were built in the Ottoman era of finely carved stone showing remarkable architectural skill.

59408028.s: One of the historical and archaeological mosques of Madinah, built in 1245 AH. It still preserves its ancient style and traditional design, and you can notice the black eastern wall, which looks striking against the white dome and forms an exceptional, eye-catching combination. It is a small mosque of about 81 square metres that receives worshippers daily, and visitors line up outside to take beautiful souvenir photos because it is a dazzling architectural and artistic masterpiece.
59408028.b: One of the historical and archaeological mosques of Madinah, built in 1245 AH. 59408028.a: 4980 Abdulrahman bin Kharif, Al Qiblatayn, Madinah

59407997.s: Visitors to Madinah are keen to visit Al Ghamamah Mosque and pray in it, as it was the last place where the Messenger (peace be upon him) led the Eid prayer. It is called "Al Ghamamah" (the Cloud) because, it is said, a cloud shielded the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) from the sun as he prayed. He also prayed the funeral prayer in absentia for the Negus (Al Najashi) there.
59407997.b:
Visitors to Madinah are keen to visit Al Ghamamah Mosque and pray in it, as it was the last place where the Messenger (peace be upon him) led the Eid prayer. It is called "Al Ghamamah" (the Cloud) because, it is said, a cloud shielded the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) from the sun as he prayed. He also prayed the funeral prayer in absentia for the Negus (Al Najashi) there.

It is only about 500 metres from the Prophet's Mosque, to its south-west. It receives many visitors these days who come to see the ancient cultural heritage it holds, and the landmarks and memories connected with the Prophet's biography.

59407899.s: Al Baqi Cemetery (Baqi Al Gharqad) is the most famous cemetery in the Islamic world and has been the main burial ground of the people of Madinah since the time of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the present day. It is named after the gharqad trees that once grew there. A large number of Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) are buried in it, most notably Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), the Mothers of the Believers, the Prophet's (peace be upon him) aunts and daughters, and his uncle Al Abbas ibn Abdulmuttalib, as well as thousands of the Tabi'un, scholars and righteous people through successive ages. It is narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to visit Al Baqi and pray for forgiveness for its people, saying: "Peace be upon you, abode of believing people; and we, God willing, will join you."
59407899.b: Al Baqi Cemetery (Baqi Al Gharqad) is the most famous cemetery in the Islamic world and has been the main burial ground of the people of Madinah since the time of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the present day. It is named after the gharqad trees that once grew there. A large number of Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) are buried in it, most notably Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), the Mothers of the Believers, the Prophet's (peace be upon him) aunts and daughters, and his uncle Al Abbas ibn Abdulmuttalib, as well as thousands of the Tabi'un, scholars and righteous people through successive ages. It is narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to visit Al Baqi and pray for forgiveness for its people, saying: "Peace be upon you, abode of believing people; and we, God willing, will join you." Al Baqi is distinguished by its simple character, free of ornament, following the Prophetic Sunnah of levelling graves. It lies next to the Prophet's Mosque on its south-eastern side, and visitors are allowed to visit it at set times.

59407895.s: Masjid Al Ijaba, also known as Masjid Bani Muawiyah, is located north-east of the Prophet's Mosque, about 385 metres north of Al Baqi on King Faisal Road. It is called Al Ijaba (the Answering) because the Prophet's (peace be upon him) supplication there was answered. It is narrated that he prayed there and made three supplications: he asked his Lord not to destroy his community through famine and drought, not to let an outside enemy overpower them and violate their sanctity, and not to make their strength be turned against one another. The first two were granted and the third was not.
59407895.b: Masjid Al Ijaba, also known as Masjid Bani Muawiyah, is located north-east of the Prophet's Mosque, about 385 metres north of Al Baqi on King Faisal Road. It is called Al Ijaba (the Answering) because the Prophet's (peace be upon him) supplication there was answered. It is narrated that he prayed there and made three supplications: he asked his Lord not to destroy his community through famine and drought, not to let an outside enemy overpower them and violate their sanctity, and not to make their strength be turned against one another. The first two were granted and the third was not. For this reason Muslims through the ages have sought blessings by visiting it and praying in it, and throughout history it has received the attention of rulers and governors who restored it and preserved its structure. It remains one of the landmarks visitors to Madinah seek out today.

59407890.s: Quba Mosque in Madinah is considered the first mosque founded by the Messenger (peace be upon him) when he arrived in Madinah as a migrant from Makkah. He took part in laying its first stones, and the Companions then completed it.
59407890.b:
Quba Mosque in Madinah is considered the first mosque founded by the Messenger (peace be upon him) when he arrived in Madinah as a migrant from Makkah. He took part in laying its first stones, and the Companions then completed it.

The Noble Messenger would visit it from time to time to pray in it, usually choosing Saturdays, and he urged people to visit it. A noble hadith says: "Whoever purifies himself in his house, then comes to Quba Mosque and prays in it, will have a reward like that of an Umrah."
59407890.a: 3493 Al Hijrah Road, Al Khatim, Madinah

59407888.s: Jabal Al Rumat (Mount of the Archers) is one of the most important historical landmarks that followers of the Prophet's biography are keen to visit, and it is also known as Mount "Aynayn". It lies south of Mount Uhud, bordered on its southern side by Wadi Qanat. The mountain gained great historical importance because the Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered fifty archers there, led by Abdullah ibn Jubayr (may Allah be pleased with him), to stay at their posts to protect the Muslims' rear during the Battle of Uhud and not to leave the mountain whatever happened.
59407888.b: Jabal Al Rumat (Mount of the Archers) is one of the most important historical landmarks that followers of the Prophet's biography are keen to visit, and it is also known as Mount "Aynayn". It lies south of Mount Uhud, bordered on its southern side by Wadi Qanat. The mountain gained great historical importance because the Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered fifty archers there, led by Abdullah ibn Jubayr (may Allah be pleased with him), to stay at their posts to protect the Muslims' rear during the Battle of Uhud and not to leave the mountain whatever happened. But when they thought victory had been achieved, most of the archers left their positions to collect spoils. Khalid ibn Al Walid, before he embraced Islam, exploited this gap and circled behind the polytheist army, which turned the tide of the battle and left the Muslims with heavy losses. Today the mountain is one of the most prominent places where this enduring lesson about the importance of obeying the commander's orders is told.
59407888.a: Jabal Al Rumat, Sayyid Al Shuhada, Madinah

59407886.s: Mount Uhud is one of the most famous historical mountains for Muslims, rising majestically over Madinah from the north, about seven kilometres long and 2 to 3 kilometres wide, and reaching a height of 350 metres. The mountain gained its great standing because it witnessed the famous Battle of Uhud in the third year of the Hijra, one of the most important battles in the Prophet's biography after Badr, in which the Muslims led by the Prophet (peace be upon him) fought the army of Quraysh at its foot. Seventy Companions were martyred in it, foremost among them Hamza ibn Abdulmuttalib, the uncle of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the Master of Martyrs. In a noble hadith the Prophet (peace be upon him) said of this mountain: "Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it."
59407886.b: Mount Uhud is one of the most famous historical mountains for Muslims, rising majestically over Madinah from the north, about seven kilometres long and 2 to 3 kilometres wide, and reaching a height of 350 metres. The mountain gained its great standing because it witnessed the famous Battle of Uhud in the third year of the Hijra, one of the most important battles in the Prophet's biography after Badr, in which the Muslims led by the Prophet (peace be upon him) fought the army of Quraysh at its foot. Seventy Companions were martyred in it, foremost among them Hamza ibn Abdulmuttalib, the uncle of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the Master of Martyrs. In a noble hadith the Prophet (peace be upon him) said of this mountain: "Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it." That is one of the Prophetic sayings that highlight its special standing. Today the mountain is one of the most prominent destinations for visitors to Madinah who want to learn the story of the battle and visit the nearby martyrs' cemetery.

59407666.s: Alhokair Time Entertainment City is in the Al Qaswa district of Madinah and is one of the city's leading family entertainment destinations. It opened in 2001 as part of the chain of amusement parks run by the Alhokair Group. The city has a variety of electric and motion rides suited to all ages, especially children, as well as a large hall of video and arcade games. It opens daily from 2:00 pm to 11:00 pm and offers a complete entertainment experience for an enjoyable evening with the family, away from the bustle of the religious sites.
59407666.b:

The city has a variety of electric and motion rides suited to all ages, especially children, as well as a large hall of video and arcade games. Visiting in the evening is recommended to avoid the daytime crowds and enjoy the atmosphere.
59407666.a: CHGP+X2, 7017 Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Branch Road, Al Qaswa, Madinah

59407635.s: Wadi Al Aqiq is the most famous valley of Madinah and a witness to its history and to the Prophet's biography. Historical writings indicate that the valley was like a permanently flowing river, and many orchards and homes were built along its banks in the past, especially in the Umayyad and Abbasid eras, including the ruins of the palaces of Saad ibn Abi Waqqas and Urwah ibn Al Zubayr.
59407635.b: Wadi Al Aqiq is the most famous valley of Madinah and a witness to its history and to the Prophet's biography. Historical writings indicate that the valley was like a permanently flowing river, and many orchards and homes were built along its banks in the past, especially in the Umayyad and Abbasid eras, including the ruins of the palaces of Saad ibn Abi Waqqas and Urwah ibn Al Zubayr.

59407631.s: The King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex in Madinah is classified as the largest Quran printing press in the world, covering an area of 250,000 square metres. It is one of the most prominent and important tourist places in Madinah, visited each year by about 2 million visitors of many countries and nationalities, most of them Umrah performers and pilgrims.
59407631.b: The King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex in Madinah is classified as the largest Quran printing press in the world, covering an area of 250,000 square metres. 59407631.a: Tabuk Branch Road, An Nakhil, Madinah

59407625.s: Aryaf Taibah farm park is a family park and tourist attraction, and one of the best parks in Madinah and tourist places in Saudi Arabia. It offers many services to its visitors, with areas set aside for family seating, restaurants, cafes, children's play areas, and shops selling dates and handmade crafts of Madinah.
